Values.Description: Acta-shipped system [Job] (a reserved name prefixed with sys.) OR Acta runtime path that decided a transition. ActorKey = "sys:{jobNamespace}:{jobName}" or "sys:{component}".

A human or admin tool acting from outside any job context (endpoint, dashboard, admin script). ActorKey carries the authenticated principal name as-is (e.g. http.User.Identity.Name); null when the host did not authenticate.
ctx.* throw-to-transition inside a user handler. ActorKey = "{jobId}".

Worker-process lifecycle (registered / heartbeat / dead-marking) AND worker-mediated hot-path actions (claim, lease renewal). ActorKey stores the acting worker's public ref as canonical lowercase uuid text; read projections render it as wrk_....
Channel accepts deliveries.
Configured but intentionally muted; matching alerts are suppressed.
Configured but decommissioned; matching alerts are suppressed.
Materialized; awaiting the first send attempt.
Send deferred until JobAlert.RetryAfterUtc instant.
Intentionally not sent because process-local channel policy rejected delivery.
Successfully sent to the channel transport.
Send attempt failed; eligible for retry by the next sys.alerts system job tick.
Alert kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
First failure in a window; emitted by Automatic origin on non-terminal failure.
Threshold-bound emission (e.g., LostClaimAlertThreshold reached).
Terminal failure; emitted by Automatic origin on Status to Failed.
Hand-raised; ctx.AlertAsync from inside a handler.
Recovery transition; emitted when a previously-failed Job succeeds.
System-emitted from a state-mutating SP (failure / timeout / orphan / deadline).
ctx.AlertAsync from inside a user handler.
No automatic failure alerts. ctx.AlertAsync still creates rows.

Default. Alerts on every failure transition; dedupe-window collapses repeats. Final exhaustion writes a separate alert (a different JobEventReasonCode yields a different DeduplicationKey). Resolves on recovery.
Informational alerts on final failure only; low severity.
Alert on terminal failure only (final exhaustion / orphan / deadline). Resolves on recovery.
Reserved for system Jobs. Emits at Severity = Critical to the Job's channel, or the configured "default" channel when none is declared.
Informational; not paging.
Non-terminal failure transition; dedupe-window collapses repeats.
Terminal failure or operator-attention event.
Highest severity; emitted by system Jobs (AlertProfile = SysCritical) and operator alerts for incidents. Whether it pages depends on the routed channel's transport and config.
Engine auto-terminates an overdue job at admission and refuses to re-arm a retry past the deadline.
Deadline is informational; the engine never auto-terminates, the handler reads ctx.IsOverdue.
Event id not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
An operator suspended a tenant; the key stops resolving at enqueue. ReasonMessage carries the reason.
An operator resumed a suspended tenant; its key resolves at enqueue again. ReasonMessage carries the reason.
An operator changed a tenant display name / description. ReasonMessage carries the reason.
An operator suspended a namespace; enqueue into it is rejected. ReasonMessage carries the reason.
An operator resumed a suspended namespace; enqueue into it is allowed again. ReasonMessage carries the reason.
An operator changed a namespace owner team / description. ReasonMessage carries the reason.
An operator changed a job definition's policy overrides; ReasonMessage summarizes the change.
Handler invocation began; paired with job.execution-finished on (JobId, ExecutionNumber).
Per-attempt outcome finalized. DurationMs / ExecutionStatusCode / JobEventReasonCode populated.
Recurring Job's NextRunAtUtc advanced to the next firing instant.
Handler called ctx.SleepAsync; the Job re-armed to Ready with the sleep timer's due instant; budget-neutral.
The job re-armed Ready with a new NextRunAtUtc: a handler reschedule or an operator RescheduleAsync; actor and reason distinguish.
Job was cancelled (Status to Cancelled, terminal).
Job was paused (Status to Paused).
Job was resumed (Status to Ready).
Job was restarted (Status to Ready; failure_count reset, retention cleared, execution_number unchanged).
Operator changed the job's claim priority; ReasonMessage carries the operator's reason, if any.
Operator hard-deleted a terminal job. job_id/job_ref are null (the row is gone); ReasonMessage carries the purged job's ref and name. Always emitted regardless of audit level.
Operator amended a job's stored input payload; Detail carries bounded JSON metadata (format name and byte count) about the previous payload and ReasonMessage carries the why.
Signal delivered via IJobs.RaiseSignalAsync; matching signal checkpoint (State = Set) UPSERTed.
Handler called ctx.ResetStateAsync; the Job's JobCheckpoint / JobStep / JobResult rows were cleared so the next execution starts as new.

Application-authored note from ctx.NoteAsync. The only event code an application can write and one the runtime never emits, so every other event stays provably system-written. ReasonMessage carries the line; Detail carries the optional JSON payload.
A recurring schedule was paused; ReasonMessage carries the schedule name.
A recurring schedule was resumed; ReasonMessage carries the schedule name.
A timed pause elapsed; the scheduler auto-resumed the schedule. ReasonMessage carries the schedule name.
Operator changed a schedule's expression/timezone overrides; ReasonMessage summarizes the change and carries the schedule name.
Operator fired a schedule manually; the slot's cursor was pulled to now. ReasonMessage carries the schedule name.
Worker process registered; a workers row was appended (Status: Active).
Worker process shut down cleanly (Status: Active/Draining to Stopped).
Worker heartbeat went stale; the sys.recovery system job flipped the worker to Dead.
Operator acknowledged an alert; ReasonMessage carries the alert id and note.
Operator manually resolved an alert; ReasonMessage carries the alert id and note.
A durable setting was written (created or overwritten); Detail carries the setting name.
An operator command returned quarantined outbox rows to Pending; ReasonMessage carries the justification and the row ids.
An operator command deleted quarantined outbox rows; ReasonMessage carries the justification and the deleted row ids.
Handler in flight.
Handler returned successfully. Resets the runtime failure count.
Handler threw RescheduleJobException; does not charge budget.
The attempt ended because the job parked: a ctx.SleepAsync timer, an awaited signal, or awaited children. Does not charge budget.
Handler threw PauseJobException.
Handler threw or ctx.Fail called. Charges failure budget.
Handler ended via cancel; does not charge budget.
Lease lapsed past grace; reclaimed by the sys.recovery system job. Charges budget.
No audit-filtered per-job events; always-on system/catalog events still emit.
Emit failed job.execution-finished only; suppress other audit-filtered per-job events.
Emit all audit-filtered per-job events. User Jobs default.
User variable slot; UPSERT, last-writer-wins, no state machine.
Signal slot; Pending while awaited, Set once raised.
Durable sleep timer; Pending until due, Consumed on replay past the due instant.
Progress slot; UPSERT, last-writer-wins, one per job.
Child terminal-outcome latch on the parent; Pending while awaited, Set when the child lands terminal.
Awaited or armed; the slot has not been satisfied yet.
Raised; the payload is stored and a waiting job proceeds.
Due instant reached; the replayed handler consumed the timer and proceeded.
Enqueue allowed; claim allowed.
Enqueue REJECTED; parked rows (Ready/Paused/Suspended) cancelled with ReasonCode = 'job.definition-retired'; in-flight executions finish their attempt.
Reason id not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
None of the system-catalog codes fit; the operator-readable story lives in ReasonMessage.
Handler threw an exception that was not raised via ctx.Fail.
Worker lease expired; the sys.recovery system job reclaimed the Job.
Execution exceeded JobDefinition.ExecutionTimeout for this attempt.
Handler threw an exception the runtime classifies as non-retryable (NotImplementedException, NotSupportedException); terminal Failed without consuming the retry budget.
Job passed its whole-job deadline; the engine terminated it Cancelled without consuming the retry budget.
Worker aborted the attempt mid-flight (lease renewal at risk, a held lock lost, or a step's ownership unconfirmed); retried under the failure budget.
Recurring slot has no live JobSchedule yielding a next instant; row is system-paused.
Operator-initiated control transition via an IJobs control verb (Cancel/Pause/Resume/Restart).
Job was cancelled because an ancestor job in its lineage was cancelled (recursive cascade).
Job was cancelled because its definition was retired by registration; parked rows (Ready/Paused/Suspended) are cancelled set-wise, in-flight executions finish their attempt.
Handler called ctx.RescheduleAsync; attempt finalized as Rescheduled.
Handler called ctx.SleepAsync or ctx.WaitSignalAsync; attempt suspended (budget-neutral) until the sleep timer's due instant or a matching signal is raised.
Handler called ctx.FailAsync; the attempt was finalized as a deliberate terminal Failed (no retry, budget untouched).
Handler called ctx.CancelAsync; the attempt was finalized as a deliberate terminal Cancelled (no retry, budget untouched).
Handler called ctx.PauseAsync; the Job was held in Paused until an external resume (budget untouched).
RaiseSignalAsync set a matching signal and moved a Suspended Job to Ready.
An inline step failed within budget (or on replay still awaits its retry instant); the parent re-armed budget-neutral until the step's next_retry_at_utc.
A claimed exclusive-key job found its key lock held at execution admission; re-armed Ready after the fixed bounce delay (budget-neutral).

An at-most-once step was re-entered on replay before its outcome was recorded (worker died mid-flight); the body is not re-run and the parent lands terminal Failed. Non-retryable; the outcome is unknown and must be reconciled externally.

The handler returned successfully but its serialized result exceeded MaxInlinePayloadBytes, so the body was dropped rather than persisted. The job still succeeded; a typed read of the missing result throws.
Worker process exited cleanly via SIGTERM / IHostedService.StopAsync.
Worker heartbeat exceeded the liveness window; the sys.recovery system job flipped Status to Dead.
Lowest practical priority; bulk-class workloads.
Default priority. Most jobs use this.
Above normal; operator opt-in for time-sensitive work.
Critical priority; close-to-realtime operator workloads.
Highest priority; always pages.
Eligible for claim; the claim path selects rows in this Status.
Parked and not progressing: awaiting an external signal via ctx.WaitSignalAsync, or awaiting children via ctx.WaitChildAsync / WaitChildrenAsync.
Not running, awaiting an external trigger to resume.
Claimed by a worker; lease active, handler invocation pending.
Handler is running. JobEvent(job.execution-started) has been appended; matching job.execution-finished pending.
Terminal success.
Terminal failure: MaxAttempts exhausted, expiration fired, or ctx.Fail called.
Terminal cancellation by IJobs.CancelAsync or ctx.Cancel.
Step in flight or retrying within MaxAttempts / RetryWindow.
Step completed successfully; Result populated (or ResultFormatId = 0 for void steps).
Step exhausted retry budget; parent handler receives StepExhaustedException.
At-most-once step was re-entered before completion; outcome is unknown (ran 0 or 1 times). Parent receives StepInterruptedException.
Jobs may carry a tenant or not; no enqueue-time tenant rule applies.
Every enqueue must carry a tenant, by explicit TenantKey or parent inheritance; a tenant-less enqueue is rejected.
An explicit TenantKey is rejected and a child never inherits its parent's tenant; rows always store tenant NULL.
After downtime, fire once immediately for all missed occurrences, then resume from the next occurrence after now.
After downtime, skip all missed occurrences and resume from the first occurrence strictly after now.
Namespace resolves at enqueue; enqueue allowed.
Enqueue into the namespace is rejected. Reversible (operator hold). Existing in-flight jobs are unaffected.
Due for relay claim; the claim path selects rows in this status once next_attempt_at_utc is reached.
Leased by a relay claim; claim_token and claim_until_utc are set until the lease finalizes or expires.
Excluded from normal claims after exhausting delivery policy or a non-recoverable contract error; requires an operator requeue or delete.
Cron expression (Cronos dialect). Set at compile time by the source generator.
Interval duration: human (e.g. "5m") or ISO 8601 (e.g. "PT5M", "P1D"). Set at compile time by the source generator.
Operator-driven schedule add/remove. No code path produces rows with this origin today.
Declared in [JobSchedule] attribute; refreshed by catalog upsert.
Schedule is eligible to fire.
Operator-paused; does not fire until resumed, or until PausedUntilUtc passes when set.
Origin declaration disappeared from the catalog; set by reconciliation. Cannot fire or be paused/resumed.
Deployment-wide setting; scope_id is NULL.
Setting scoped to one namespace; scope_id = namespaces.id.
Setting scoped to one job definition; scope_id = definitions.id.
Tag attached to one tenant.
Tag attached to one namespace.
Tag attached to one job definition.
Tag attached to one job.
Tag attached to one schedule.
Tag attached to one worker.
Tag attached to one alert.
Tag attached to one event.
Tenant key resolves at enqueue; enqueue allowed.

Admission suspended: new enqueues naming the tenant key are rejected, while already admitted jobs keep running and may expand through inherited children. Applies to enqueue transactions beginning after the suspend commits. Reversible (billing/abuse hold, admin pause).
Polling claim; accepting work.
Worker stopped polling; finishing in-flight.
Worker shut down cleanly; terminal success.
Worker is dead; the sys.recovery system job reclaims leases.
